notes: LANDED 2026-08-09 (PB60): BindNumvalCFamily walks ( argument-1 [argument-2] [ANYCASE] ) BY POSITION - the CONVERT-5a template. Slot 0 always binds as argument-1 (ANYCASE is 8.10 context-sensitive, so a data item so named stays legal there - written before argument-1 it now binds as an operand, fails name resolution and the arity screen, both measured); ANYCASE is admitted once, last, and a repeat or a trailing operand rejects COBOL1504 (negative pb60-numvalc-anycase-position; the old order-free sweep accepted NUMVAL-C(ANYCASE WS-A "USD") and a doubled ANYCASE). The LOCALE phrase keeps its upstream 4.2.7 documented-non-support interception (COBOL1518). Editions field stays 2002+ (the function's own introduction; Annex E is informative). retired-witness: conformance-test:CorpusRunnerTests.EnabledNegativeCase_RejectsWithItsDiagnostic (kb/Work PB3177 replaced the corpus runner with the conformance suite's: the refusal is asserted by ConformanceSuiteTests.WiseOwlRefusal_RefusesTheSourceWithItsDiagnostic) kb/Work PB4359 (2026-11-01): the ANYCASE bracket is a 2002 introduction (printed in ISO/IEC 1989:2002 15.55 / 15.76; ANYCASE reserved from 2002) - the construct row numval-c-anycase-keyword-2002 gates it in BindNumvalCFamily, COBOL0900 at 85 (pb4359-numval-c-anycase-below-2002; TEST-NUMVAL-C is itself a 2002 function), accepted from 2002 (pb4359_numval_c_anycase_2002). || editions corrected from 2002,2014,2023 to 85,2002,2014,2023 (kb/Work PB3321, the reading of a clause 15 rule's band; kb/Work PB3173's late starts re-read against each edition's own text): the general format FUNCTION NUMVAL-C ( argument-1 [ argument-2 ] ) is §1989:A.2.30.2's format at 85; 2002 adds the ANYCASE and LOCALE phrases, which do not move the format's start, the same reading as FMT-15.57.2 (LOWER-CASE, whose LOCALE phrase is 2014) and FMT-15.50.2 (LENGTH, whose PHYSICAL phrase is 2014). The phrases' own rules start at their editions (AR-15.68.3-5, RV-15.68.4-3, kb/Work PB3321).
